value.note: JollyChef states 1.3-1.5 dinner plates/guest for a buffet and 1.5 cups+cutlery/guest. The authored 1.5 sets/guest sits at that figure; value NOT changed. LIMITATION: the source recommends 3 napkins/guest, more than one set provides. CAVEAT: vendor-published and commercially interested in a higher multiplier - trade consensus among sellers, not independent corroboration.
Per-guest crab quantity grounded to the WebstaurantStore protein portion guide (fetched 2026-07-16).

Reddy Ice states 1-2 lb of ice per person; its own worked outdoor-BBQ example computes to 2.1 lb/guest. A Crab Feast is an outdoor summer cook, so the outdoor case applies and the authored 2 lb/guest sits at that figure. Value unchanged; provenance only. CAVEAT: a packaged-ice manufacturer profits from a higher figure, so treat 2 lb as ceiling-leaning planning guidance.

bar-provision-2026 states ice ~1.5 lb/guest (12-15 bags per 100) as standard US party drink provisioning. Dinner Party is the indoor baseline case, and the authored 1.5 matches the source-stated rate exactly. Value unchanged; provenance only.

Reddy Ice states 1-2 lb of ice per person. Fish Fry authors 1.5 lb/guest, which sits inside that stated range; the value is NOT changed here. CAVEAT: a packaged-ice manufacturer profits from a higher figure, so treat the range as ceiling-leaning planning guidance rather than a measured mean.

DERIVATION CORRECTED (Phase 5C.2, supersedes v1). bar-provision-2026 states ~1/2 bottle of wine per DRINKING guest (~1 bottle per ~2.5 drinking guests per hour; a 750ml pours ~5 servings). This line is expressed per GUEST, so the sourced 0.5/drinker is multiplied by an assumed ~80% drinking rate for an older mixed daytime crowd: 0.5 x 0.8 = 0.4 bottle/guest. The ~80% rate is an ASSUMPTION, not sourced, and is the one unverified step. WITHDRAWN FROM v1: "wine carries ~40% of the drink load" was wrong twice - the source assigns ~40% to BEER (beer+wine ~75%, implying wine ~35%), and v1's own arithmetic (3h x 1/h x 40% / 5 glasses) yields 0.24 bottle/guest, not the 0.4 it published. The VALUE survives; only the reasoning was defective.
value.claim: Source states ~1/2 bottle of wine per drinking guest at ~1 drink/guest/hour; at an assumed ~80% drinking rate for an older daytime crowd this yields ~0.4 bottle per guest
value.sufficientWhen: A drinking-participation rate for older daytime retirement gatherings confirms the ~80% assumption, OR wine consumption data from >=2 comparable 3h events confirms ~0.4 bottle/guest when beer/seltzer is also present
